children.text: Shopping for an Office 2024 Professional Plus key, you will run into three conflicting stories: stores selling cheap lifetime keys, Microsoft documentation describing something called Office LTSC 2024, and app lists that cannot agree on Publisher or Teams. This guide sorts it out using Microsoft's own documentation.

Below you will find the exact app list, how the license differs from consumer editions such as Home & Business 2024, what support ending in 2029 means in practice, and how to buy a genuine key without overpaying.
What Is Office 2024 Professional Plus?
Office 2024 Professional Plus is the informal name for
Office LTSC Professional Plus 2024
, the top edition of Microsoft's volume-licensed Office suite. LTSC stands for Long Term Servicing Channel: the apps receive security fixes, but they never gain new features after launch.

Microsoft released it on September 18, 2024, alongside Office LTSC Standard 2024, Project 2024, and Visio LTSC 2024. The target audience is organizations - hospitals, factories, labs, public agencies - that run PCs in restricted or offline environments and need the feature set frozen for years at a time.

Because Microsoft distributes this edition through volume licensing rather than retail boxes, individual buyers usually meet it through resellers offering single keys. That is why Professional Plus listings look nothing like Office Home 2024 or Office Home & Business 2024, the consumer editions sold directly by Microsoft.
Which Apps Are Included in Office 2024 Professional Plus?
According to Microsoft's overview, Office LTSC Professional Plus 2024 ships six desktop applications for Windows:
Word 2024
for documents
Excel 2024
for spreadsheets and data analysis
PowerPoint 2024
for presentations
Outlook 2024
for email, contacts, and calendars
OneNote
for notes
Access 2024
for databases - the app that separates Professional Plus from Standard
Skype for Business is also available as an optional component during installation, which matters mainly to organizations still running on-premises phone systems.
What's Not Included
Just as important is what Microsoft left out of the 2024 LTSC release:
Publisher
- dropped from Office LTSC 2024 entirely, ahead of
its retirement after October 2026
Teams
- not preinstalled; download it separately if you need it
Copilot and AI assistance
- LTSC contains none of the cloud-backed intelligent features
Real-time co-authoring
- files stay local; there is no cloud-connected collaboration

Be skeptical of outdated store listings that promise Publisher included. Microsoft explicitly removed Publisher from this release, so a listing advertising Publisher 2024 describes a suite that does not exist - usually a sign to shop elsewhere.
What's New Compared to Office 2021
Professional Plus 2024 condenses roughly three years of updates that Microsoft 365 users already had:
Dynamic charts and more than a dozen new text and array functions in Excel
Faster, more precise search and improved meeting creation in Outlook
Better accessibility checking across the suite
Insert photos into Word, Excel, and PowerPoint straight from an Android phone
OpenDocument Format 1.4 support, with ActiveX controls disabled by default for safety

Professional Plus vs Home & Business 2024
Office 2024 Home & Business

is the closest consumer cousin: a one-time purchase that includes Outlook, permits commercial use, and lists at $249.99 direct from Microsoft. It lacks Access, activates through your Microsoft account instead of a volume-style key, and runs on both PC and Mac.

For most freelancers and small offices, Home & Business is the more practical choice thanks to simpler activation and the Mac option. Note that Professional Plus does not exist for macOS - if you are equipping a Mac, Licendi sells

Professional Plus vs Microsoft 365

A Microsoft 365 subscription buys continuously updated apps, 1 TB of OneDrive storage per person, Copilot eligibility, and installs across many devices. A perpetual license buys certainty: one payment, one frozen feature set, zero surprises. We compare both in detail in
Microsoft 365 vs Office 2024
How the Perpetual License Works
You pay once, install the suite on one Windows PC, and own it outright. There are no monthly fees and no expiry date on the software itself - but there are dates you should know:
Security updates run through October 9, 2029, per Microsoft's
official lifecycle listing
There is no Extended Support phase
- patching stops completely on that date
The apps keep working after support ends, but running unpatched Office on an internet-connected PC is a real security risk
There is no discounted upgrade path - the next perpetual release will cost full price
Five years of support is shorter than the ten-year cycles older Office releases enjoyed. If you buy in 2026, treat late 2029 as your planning horizon for the next move.
System Requirements
Office LTSC 2024 runs on current Windows platforms. Check your machine against Microsoft's published minimums before you buy:
Operating systems: Windows 11, Windows 11 LTSC 2024, Windows 10 LTSC 2021 or 2019, Windows Server 2025 or 2022. Regular Windows 10 reached end of support in October 2025, so plan for Windows 11
Processor: 1.1 GHz dual-core or faster; Arm-based devices require Windows 11
Memory and storage: 4 GB of RAM and 4 GB of free disk space
Display: 1280 x 768 minimum; the 64-bit version is required for 4K and higher resolutions
How Activation Works
Activation takes a few minutes whether your key is set up for online or phone activation:
Buy the key and receive it by email together with download links and instructions.
Uninstall any previous Office version first; older MSI-based installations are removed automatically during setup.
Install the suite and open any app, such as Word.
Enter your product key when prompted, or complete phone activation if your key uses it.
Activate once over the internet - after that, the suite works fully offline.
Keep the delivery email. Volume-style keys are not attached to a Microsoft account, so the key itself is your proof of ownership if you ever need to reinstall.
Where to Buy Office 2024 Professional Plus Safely

Price context helps you judge listings. Microsoft's consumer list prices are $149.99 for Office Home 2024 and $249.99 for Home & Business 2024, while volume-channel pricing for LTSC Professional Plus runs to hundreds of dollars per seat with five-license minimums. Deep discounts on single keys are therefore normal - and seller quality varies just as much.
Before you buy anywhere, run through this checklist:
Instant delivery with clear download and activation instructions
A refund or replacement policy if the key fails to activate
Support you can actually reach when something goes wrong
Accurate naming - honest listings say LTSC and Windows-only; vague ones hide the details
Reviews you can verify outside the seller's own website

Office 2024 Professional Plus FAQ
Does Office 2024 Professional Plus include Access?
Yes. Access 2024 is included and is the main difference from Office LTSC Standard 2024. Skype for Business can also be added during setup.
Does it include Publisher or Teams?
No. Microsoft excluded Publisher from Office LTSC 2024 ahead of its retirement after October 2026, and Teams is not preinstalled - it is a separate download.
Is there a Mac version of Professional Plus?
No. Professional Plus 2024 is Windows-only. On macOS, volume customers get Office LTSC Standard for Mac 2024, while individuals can buy Office Home & Business 2024 for Mac.
Can I use it without an internet connection?
Yes. You need internet to download, install, and activate, but after activation the apps run fully offline - and LTSC has no cloud-dependent features to miss.
How long will it receive updates?
Security updates continue until October 9, 2029. After that date the software keeps working but receives no patches, so plan your next upgrade before then.
Is Professional Plus worth it for home users?

Usually not. If you do not need Access or a frozen feature set, Office Home & Business 2024 or a Microsoft 365 subscription gives you an easier activation experience, a Mac option, and account-based reinstalls.
